==================================================
APPROVED ARCHITECTURE / BUSINESS DECISIONS
==================================================

Preserve these unless the actual approved specs or repository prove a
conflict.

1. Java 21.

2. Existing MySQL datasource is the authoritative system of record.
   Do NOT alter spring.datasource.*.

3. PostgreSQL/PGVector is for the vector store only.
   PGVector configuration belongs under:
   bootcamp.support-ticket.rag.pgvector.*

   Configuration/properties exist, but the actual PGVector DataSource /
   PgVectorStore runtime implementation has NOT yet been built.

4. Spring AI dependency/config foundation exists.

5. Ollama runtime/model wiring has NOT yet been implemented/verified.

6. SupportTicket inherited JPA @Version is the authoritative ticket
   knowledge version.

7. TicketIndexingState inherited @Version is only the optimistic-lock
   version of the indexing-state row.
   Never use it as ticket knowledge version.

8. requestedVersion and indexedVersion refer to SupportTicket knowledge
   versions.

9. Searchable ticket changes use:

   authoritative MySQL mutation
   → flush ticket so resulting SupportTicket.version is available
   → TicketIndexingState PENDING in the SAME MySQL transaction
   → requestedVersion = resulting SupportTicket.version
   → commit
   → Spring application event consumed with
      @TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT)
   → SupportTicketIndexingProcessor boundary

10. Current SupportTicketIndexingProcessor implementation is deliberately
    NO-OP.
    Do not introduce embedding/chunking/PGVector/Ollama behavior until the
    appropriate task requires it.

11. PENDING supersession:
    - requestedVersion updated
    - status = PENDING
    - indexedVersion preserved
    - attemptCount reset to 0
    - lastAttemptAt cleared
    - lastError cleared

12. Option B same-value PATCH semantics:

    A non-empty request where all supplied effective values equal existing
    values is a successful no-op:
    - no entity mutation
    - no deliberate ticket version bump
    - no indexing-state modification
    - no indexing event

    Mixed same-value + changed fields = one normal searchable change.

13. Validation occurs before comparison and before mutation.

14. Assignee equality is based on persistent User id.

15. CLOSED/CANCELLED mutations reject with:
    TERMINAL_TICKET_READ_ONLY

16. Invalid non-terminal status transitions reject with:
    INVALID_TICKET_STATUS_TRANSITION

17. Exactly five status transitions are allowed:

    OPEN → IN_PROGRESS
    IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED
    RESOLVED → CLOSED
    OPEN → CANCELLED
    IN_PROGRESS → CANCELLED

18. No resolution prerequisite exists for a transition unless the approved
    specification explicitly requires it.

19. API responses currently use:
    assigneeId + assigneeDisplay

    Null assignee:
    assigneeDisplay = "UNASSIGNED"

20. Comment author uses UserVO.forAudit.

21. AI request maximum is configurable:

    bootcamp.support-ticket.rag.ask.max-question-length

    Current default = 2000 characters.

    This is a request-size guardrail, not an embedding-model token/context
    claim.

22. Servlet context is /api.
    Ticket controller mapping is /tickets.

    Therefore external path:
    /api/tickets

    Never create /api/api/tickets.

23. Ticket authorization convention:
    @PreAuthorize("@userAuthorizationService.isUser()")

24. HTTP/domain exception mapping remains deferred to API-003.
    Some ticket domain exceptions may currently fall through to generic
    HTTP 500.

25. Gradle test and testClasses remain intentionally disabled.
    Existing tests have only been compile-verified.

## 2. Exact next task

**TASK-API-003 — Reuse authentication and global error handling**

---

## 3. Why this is next

From `spec/tasks.md` ordering and dependencies:

- Completed: FND-001–004, DOM-001–003, STM-001–002, SVC-001–003, API-001–002, QRY-001–002
- **API-003** depends on **API-002** → satisfied
- **QRY-003** (backend checkpoint) depends on QRY-001, QRY-002, **and API-003** → blocked until API-003 finishes

So API-003 is the next incomplete task — not QRY-003, and not Phase 7/RAG.

Domain exception Javadoc and `SupportTicketDomainErrorTaxonomy` explicitly defer HTTP mapping to API-003. Controllers already use `@PreAuthorize("@userAuthorizationService.isUser()")`; the missing work is mainly stable HTTP/error-envelope mapping (today those exceptions hit the generic `Exception` handler → **500**).

---

## 4. Objective

Secure ticket APIs with existing auth conventions and map ticket domain errors to the approved HTTP statuses and UI-safe `CommonResponseVO` envelopes so no ticket endpoint is accidentally public and domain failures no longer fall through as opaque 500s.

---

## 5. Requirement / AC / NFR IDs

From the task and related specs:

- **FR-016, FR-018, FR-025**
- **NFR-006**
- **AC-016** (plus AC-006/AC-007 via transition/terminal HTTP contracts)

Supporting contract: `api-contract.md` §5–§9, `state-machine.md` §5, `test-strategy.md` §3, `.cursor/rules/api-standards.mdc` / `java-springboot.mdc`.

---

## 6. Dependencies

| Dependency | Status |
|---|---|
| TASK-API-002 (`/tickets` controller) | Satisfied — `SupportTicketController` present with six endpoints |
| Domain exceptions / taxonomy (SVC-003) | Satisfied — typed exceptions + deferred HTTP notes |
| Existing `GlobalExceptionHandler`, JWT/auth handlers, `isUser()` | Present — to be extended/reused, not replaced |

---

## 7. Existing implementation to reuse

- `SupportTicketController` — already `@PreAuthorize("@userAuthorizationService.isUser()")` on all six methods; mapping `/tickets` under servlet `/api`
- `UserAuthorizationService.isUser()` / existing JWT + `AuthenticationFailureHandler` / `CustomAccessDeniedHandler`
- `GlobalExceptionHandler` — already maps `EntityNotFoundException`→404, `ConstraintViolationException`/`MethodArgumentNotValidException`→400, auth/access-denied via existing handlers
- Domain types: `InvalidTicketStatusTransitionException`, `TerminalTicketReadOnlyException`, `SupportTicketOptimisticLockException`, `SupportTicketDomainErrorTaxonomy`
- Envelope: `CommonResponseVO` (`data` + `errors: Set<String>` only — no separate code field)
- Message keys: `not.found`, `internal.server.error` in `messages_en.properties`
- Compile-only test style (e.g. `SupportTicketControllerMappingTest`, `SupportTicketDomainErrorTaxonomyTest`) — runtime `test`/`testClasses` still disabled

---

## 8. Exact behavior required

| Failure | HTTP | Envelope content |
|---|---|---|
| Invalid non-terminal transition | **400** | Stable code `INVALID_TICKET_STATUS_TRANSITION`; message includes current + requested status |
| Terminal mutation (patch/comment/status) | **409** | Stable code `TERMINAL_TICKET_READ_ONLY` |
| Optimistic lock (`TICKET_OPTIMISTIC_LOCK_CONFLICT`) | **409** | UI-safe message; no SQL/stack leakage |
| Missing/soft-deleted ticket | **404** | Existing `EntityNotFoundException` path |
| Bean Validation / constraint / empty patch / bad assignee | **400** | Existing validation handlers |
| Unauthenticated / forbidden | **401 / 403** | Existing security handlers — do not invent new roles |
| Unexpected / dependency errors | **500 / 503** | Sanitized; no credentials, SQL, stack traces, raw provider payloads |

Auth: every ticket endpoint requires an authenticated existing user via current `@PreAuthorize` convention. No new role model.

Indexing: rejected transitions/mutations must continue to leave MySQL + indexing intent unchanged (already enforced in service; API-003 must not weaken that).

---

## 9. Expected files to create/modify

**Likely modify**
- `src/main/java/.../exception/handler/GlobalExceptionHandler.java` — handlers for the three ticket domain exceptions (and any agreed 500 sanitization)
- Possibly exception Javadoc that still says “deferred to API-003”
- Possibly `SupportTicketDomainErrorTaxonomy` comments once mapping is decided

**Likely add (compile-verified until TST-002)**
- Handler / controller error-mapping tests (MockMvc or focused handler unit tests)
- Auth annotation / security-contract tests for ticket endpoints (authenticated / unauthenticated / forbidden)

**Unlikely / avoid**
- Changing `CommonResponseVO` shape unless human approves
- New auth roles, security filter stack rewrites, `/ai/ask`, enabling Gradle `test`

---

## 10. Transaction / indexing implications

None for happy-path writes. API-003 is HTTP/auth mapping only.

Must preserve: domain rejections still cause **no** ticket mutation, **no** `PENDING` intent, **no** AFTER_COMMIT indexing start. Indexing failure after commit remains unrelated to ticket-write HTTP success (FR-022) — not introduced here.

---

## 11. RAG implications

None for this task. No PGVector, embedding, Ollama, or `/api/ai/ask`. `503` dependency mapping for AI may be mentioned in specs but AI outage paths are not implementable until later RAG/AI tasks.

---

## 12. Required tests / verification

Per task + `test-strategy.md` §3 + testing rule:

- Map invalid transition → 400 + stable code + statuses in message
- Map terminal mutation → 409 + `TERMINAL_TICKET_READ_ONLY` for each mutation endpoint type
- Map optimistic conflict → 409 + safe message
- Confirm 404/400 paths still use existing handlers
- Auth: endpoints not public; unauthenticated/forbidden follow existing handlers
- Assert no sensitive leakage in 500 path for covered cases
- **Do not** enable or run Gradle `test`/`testClasses` in this phase (remain compile-verify only, same as prior tasks)

---

- QRY-003 human checkpoint
- TST-001–004 / enabling JUnit execution

## 14. Genuine human decisions / ambiguities

Specs already fix statuses and stable codes. Real open points:

1. **How stable codes appear in `CommonResponseVO`**  
   Envelope is only `errors: Set<String>`. Taxonomy explicitly leaves serialization to API-003. Options that fit without changing the VO: put `ERROR_CODE` as a set member, and/or include code + message as separate strings. Prefer confirmation if you want a strict UI contract.

2. **Sanitizing the existing catch-all `Exception` handler**  
   It currently returns `e.getMessage()` as 500. NFR-006 / task ask for sanitized 500/503. Changing the global catch-all affects all Bootcamp APIs; ticket-only handlers are safer unless you approve a global sanitize using `internal.server.error`.

3. **`503` in this task**  
   No ticket RAG dependency failure surface exists yet. Reasonable scope: map ticket domain errors + keep/tighten 500 sanitization; defer AI `503` until `/api/ai/ask`.

No other manufactured decisions — auth expression, HTTP codes, and terminal/transition semantics are already approved.

and:

    "TICKET_OPTIMISTIC_LOCK_CONFLICT",
    "<safe optimistic-conflict message>"
}

Do not introduce a new response-envelope field solely for errorCode.

Preserve deterministic output as much as the existing CommonResponseVO /
collection implementation permits.

2. HTTP STATUS MAPPING

Implement the approved mappings:

- InvalidTicketStatusTransitionException
  → HTTP 400
  → INVALID_TICKET_STATUS_TRANSITION + safe message

- TerminalTicketReadOnlyException
  → HTTP 409
  → TERMINAL_TICKET_READ_ONLY + safe message

- SupportTicketOptimisticLockException
  → HTTP 409
  → TICKET_OPTIMISTIC_LOCK_CONFLICT + safe message

Preserve existing mappings for:
- EntityNotFoundException → 404
- validation failures → 400
- existing authentication / authorization handling → 401 / 403

Do not duplicate domain rules in the handler.

3. GLOBAL CATCH-ALL

Do NOT perform a broad application-wide redesign of GlobalExceptionHandler.

Inspect the existing catch-all behavior carefully.

If sanitizing it to the project's existing generic
"internal.server.error" message is clearly safe and consistent with existing
project conventions, make the smallest correction necessary to satisfy
NFR-006.

However:

- do not expose raw exception messages, SQL, credentials, stack traces,
  provider payloads, or internal implementation details;
- do not redesign unrelated API error behavior;
- do not introduce new global response structures.

If changing the catch-all would materially alter unrelated Bootcamp API
contracts, leave that broader change out of API-003 and explicitly report
the limitation.

4. HTTP 503

Do NOT invent an AI/RAG 503 mapping now.

There is no implemented RAG dependency failure surface yet.
Handle that when the relevant AI/RAG API task introduces such failures.

5. AUTHENTICATION / AUTHORIZATION

Reuse the existing security model.

Verify all six ticket endpoints remain protected by the existing:

@PreAuthorize("@userAuthorizationService.isUser()")

Do not:
- create new roles;
- modify the JWT/security architecture;
- redesign AuthenticationFailureHandler;
- redesign CustomAccessDeniedHandler.

Only make a change if inspection proves a real API-003 defect.

6. TRANSACTION / INDEXING SAFETY

API-003 must not change:

- SupportTicketService write ordering
- Option B same-value PATCH semantics
- TicketStatusTransitionPolicy
- TerminalTicketMutationGuard
- SupportTicketIndexingIntentService
- PENDING semantics
- requestedVersion/indexedVersion semantics
- AFTER_COMMIT listener
- NoOpSupportTicketIndexingProcessor

Rejected HTTP/domain operations must continue producing:
- no successful ticket mutation
- no indexing intent
- no indexing processing event

7. TESTS

Add focused test sources for API-003.

Cover at minimum:

- invalid transition → 400
  - stable code present
  - safe message present
  - current/requested status represented as required

- terminal mutation → 409
  - TERMINAL_TICKET_READ_ONLY
  - safe message

- optimistic conflict → 409
  - TICKET_OPTIMISTIC_LOCK_CONFLICT
  - safe message
  - no internal exception/cause leakage

- existing missing ticket → 404 behavior remains intact

- existing validation → 400 behavior remains intact

- ticket endpoints remain protected by the existing authorization expression

- catch-all does not expose sensitive/raw exception details if it is changed

Do NOT enable or run Gradle test/testClasses.

Use JDK 21 explicitly:

export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"

Run only the approved compile verification:
- compileJava
- compileTestJava

8. SCOPE

Do NOT implement:
- QRY-003
- TST-*
- RAG infrastructure
- PGVector
- Ollama
- embeddings
- indexing processor behavior
- /api/ai/ask
- frontend
- E2E
- unrelated security refactors

Do not modify .specstory/**.

9. BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION

First inspect:
- GlobalExceptionHandler
- CommonResponseVO
- AuthenticationFailureHandler
- CustomAccessDeniedHandler
- SupportTicketController
- the three ticket domain exceptions
- SupportTicketDomainErrorTaxonomy
- relevant API/error/security specs

Make only changes genuinely required by TASK-API-003.

10. AFTER IMPLEMENTATION

Do NOT commit immediately.

STOP and report:

1. files created
2. files modified
3. exact exception → HTTP mappings
4. exact CommonResponseVO error representation
5. authentication/authorization verification
6. whether the global catch-all was changed and why
7. sanitization behavior
8. tests added/updated
9. compileJava result
10. compileTestJava result
11. git diff/status
12. confirmation that SVC-002 indexing behavior was untouched
13. deviations, limitations, or concerns

Then STOP for human review.

Do not start QRY-003 or any later task.

> **Affected:** Test proposal/review evidence; then approved `src/test/java` files.

| **Status transition** | Policy matrix + service legal/illegal/terminal transition tests |

# STOP — explanation only (no further changes / no runs)

Note: the interrupted prior edit already left `@AutoConfigureMockMvc(addFilters = false)` and a slim method-security config in `SupportTicketControllerWebMvcTest.java`. This report explains that proposal; **no additional edits are made here.**

---

## 1. Why it failed after `TestPropertySource`

After fixing the circular placeholder, context load progressed past property binding, then failed for a **different** root cause:

**Exact root cause (last successful diagnosis with filters still enabled):**

```text
org.springframework.beans.factory.NoSuchBeanDefinitionException:
No qualifying bean of type 'org.springframework.security.authentication.AuthenticationManager' available

Error creating bean with name 'jwtValidationFilter'
… Unsatisfied dependency expressed through constructor parameter 0:
No qualifying bean of type 'org.springframework.security.authentication.AuthenticationManager'
```

**Meaning:** the `@WebMvcTest` slice, with servlet security filters still in play, attempted to create Bootcamp’s real `JwtValidationFilter`, which requires a production `AuthenticationManager` (and the rest of JWT/security wiring). That bean set is **not** present in a controller slice, so the ApplicationContext failed before any assertions ran.

*(Earlier transient causes in the same session, not the post-`TestPropertySource` root issue: circular `spring.autoconfigure.exclude`; then Mockito/ByteBuddy agent attach under sandbox.)*

---

## 2. Why `addFilters = false` was proposed

With filters **on**, MockMvc exercises the **servlet SecurityFilterChain**, which in this app pulls in `JwtValidationFilter` → `AuthenticationManager` / JWT providers. Wiring that correctly means either:

- importing a large slice of real `SecurityConfiguration` + JWT beans, or  
- inventing test doubles that **are** a security model.

`addFilters = false` avoids constructing/running those filters so the slice can test **controller + validation + exception advice** without assembling the full JWT stack.

It is a **test-slice scoping choice**, not a production security change.

---

## 3. What the proposed edit changed (strategy)

Conceptually (the interrupted patch):

**Removed (~security-filter strategy):** custom `SecurityFilterChain` bean that `securityMatcher`’d `/tickets/**`, `permitAll`, CSRF off, and wired `AuthenticationEntryPoint` / `AccessDeniedHandler` into the **filter chain**.

**Added (~method-security / advice strategy):**

- `@AutoConfigureMockMvc(addFilters = false)`
- empty `@EnableMethodSecurity` nested config only
- comments stating filters are off and JWT wiring is avoided

That switches “401/403 via ExceptionTranslationFilter / filter chain” → “rely on `@PreAuthorize` + `GlobalExceptionHandler` (and possibly no real filter-chain 401/403).”

---

## 4. What is still genuinely proven with filters disabled

| Concern | Proven with `addFilters = false`? |
|---|---|
| Request mapping (`/tickets`…) | **Yes** (DispatcherServlet → controller) |
| Bean Validation → 400 | **Yes** (`@Valid` / advice) |
| `CommonResponseVO` / `ListResponseVO` | **Yes** (serialized body) |
| Domain exception → HTTP (400/409/404 + `errors`) | **Yes** (`GlobalExceptionHandler` + mocked service throws) |
| `@PreAuthorize` expression evaluation | **Partially** — method security can still run **if** `@EnableMethodSecurity` is on and a security context / SpEL beans exist |
| Unauthenticated → **401 via real filter chain** | **No** |
| Forbidden → **403 via real filter chain** | **No** |

Do **not** claim filter-chain 401/403 from this slice if filters are off.

---

## 5. Explicit non-claim

If filters are disabled, this WebMvcTest **does not** prove 401/403 through the real Spring Security **filter chain** (`JwtValidationFilter`, `ExceptionTranslationFilter`, production `SecurityFilterChain`).

---

## 6. How TST-002 can still runtime-test the real `/api/tickets` security contract

Without inventing roles/JWT semantics or weakening production config:

1. Keep **controller / validation / domain-error** MockMvc with filters off (or an equally lightweight slice).  
2. Add a **dedicated security MockMvc** (or narrow `@SpringBootTest` + MockMvc) with **filters enabled**, that:
   - uses existing `SecurityConfiguration` behavior (`permitAll` at HTTP + method `@PreAuthorize`),
   - supplies only the **minimum real beans** needed for `JwtValidationFilter` / `AuthenticationManager` **or** uses Spring Security Test against that real chain without rewriting auth,
   - asserts:
     - no authentication → **401** via existing `JwtAuthenticationFailureHandler` / entry-point path used in production,
     - authenticated but `isUser() == false` → **403** via `CustomAccessDeniedHandler`,
     - `isUser() == true` → request reaches controller.

Production already separates **filter-level permitAll** from **method-level `isUser()`**. Tests should mirror that, not replace it.

---

## 7. `SupportTicketControllerAuthorizationTest`

**Reflection / annotation-only.**  
It checks all six mapped methods have  
`@PreAuthorize("@userAuthorizationService.isUser()")`.  
It is **not** a runtime security/HTTP test.

---

## 8. Smallest correct arrangement (recommendation)

**Split (acceptable and preferred here):**

| Suite | Filters | Proves |
|---|---|---|
| `SupportTicketControllerWebMvcTest` | **off** (`addFilters = false`) | mappings, validation, envelopes, domain→HTTP |
| New `SupportTicketControllerSecurityWebMvcTest` (name TBD) | **on**, minimal real security wiring | runtime 401 / 403 / allowed `isUser()` for `/tickets` |
| Existing `SupportTicketControllerAuthorizationTest` | N/A | annotation presence only |

**Do not:**

- change production security,  
- weaken expected 401/403,  
- claim filter-chain auth from a filters-off slice,  
- invent a new role/JWT model for green tests.

---

**STOP for human review.** Await approval of the split (or an alternate “filters-on with minimal real wiring” approach) before any further code or test runs.

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET,glob
total=fail=skip=err=0
failures=[]
for f in glob.glob('build/test-results/test/TEST-*.xml'):
    root=ET.parse(f).getroot()
    total += int(root.get('tests') or 0)
    fail += int(root.get('failures') or 0)
    err += int(root.get('errors') or 0)
    skip += int(root.get('skipped') or 0)
    for tc in root.findall('testcase'):
        fe = tc.find('failure')
        if fe is None:
            fe = tc.find('error')
        if fe is not None:
            failures.append((root.get('name'), tc.get('name'), fe.get('message') or ''))
print(f'total={total} passed={total-fail-err-skip} failed={fail+err} skipped={skip}')
for suite,name,msg in failures:
    print(f'FAIL: {suite} :: {name}')
print('\nTicket suites:')
for f in sorted(glob.glob('build/test-results/test/TEST-*.xml')):
    name=ET.parse(f).getroot().get('name') or ''
    if any(k in name for k in ('ticket','Ticket','SupportTicket','GlobalExceptionHandlerSupport','TicketStatus','TerminalTicket','TicketIndexing')):
        root=ET.parse(f).getroot()
        t,fai,sk=int(root.get('tests') or 0),int(root.get('failures') or 0),int(root.get('skipped') or 0)
        print(f'  {name}: {t} tests, {fai} fail, {sk} skip')
PY
```

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
`created_by` allows null values. This supports tests without security context.

A MySQLContainer-based abstract test base will use @SpringBootTest with webEnvironment NONE and @DynamicPropertySource for datasource properties. Redis, Quartz, AWS, and other external services will be disabled. A Recording spy bean will replace SupportTicketIndexingProcessor. Required User fields for assignee tests include firstName, email, externalId, employeeCode, and roles. competency_id and related fields are nullable.

Quartz JDBC job storage may fail if the Liquibase changelog is inactive. The test base will exclude QuartzAutoConfiguration or switch to memory job store. Redis auto-configuration beans will also be excluded. The circular dependency placeholder for these exclusions will be set explicitly inside DynamicPropertySource.

JWT secrets may be needed to prevent SecurityConfiguration failures during tests. Testcontainers requires Docker, so ryuk is unavailable without it. The plan is to create a `SupportTicketMysqlTestcontainersSupport` base class, plus separate `SupportTicketMysqlPersistenceIT` and `SupportTicketMysqlTransactionIT` integration tests. Rollback and AFTER_COMMIT verification will use `TransactionTemplate` or `PlatformTransactionManager` injected into the test class.

The rollback test will verify that mutations and intents are fully reverted. It will create a ticket, record its original title and version, then force a transaction rollback. Afterward it will assert that the ticket still holds the original title and that no new intent was persisted.

After creation, the ticket carries a PENDING intent at version V. A rolled-back update keeps the title unchanged and leaves the indexing state at V, so the processor is not invoked for that mutation. AFTER_COMMIT events fire only for committed updates; a rolled-back update does not trigger the processor again. The recording spy bean will be declared as a primary test configuration bean.

Optimistic locking will be verified by loading the same ticket in two separate EntityManagers. One update will flush and bump the version. The second update will then fail on flush because the version has changed. Using the repository or service layer directly is too complex for this proof.

Keyword search tests will use unique terms per field. Case-insensitive matching is expected, for example "Foo" against "foo" in the title. The list endpoint DTO and default sort constant also need inspection. If Docker is unavailable, the tests will be implemented and attempted, with the Docker daemon failure reported accurately. Coverage documentation will note that the sources were authored but runtime execution remains blocked, rather than claiming proven behavior.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
PropertyInitializer only executes from main(), not from @SpringBootTest.

QuartzAutoConfiguration may fail without QRTZ tables during tests. Quartz and Redis should be excluded in test properties. The test class needs `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = NONE)`, `@Import(RecordingProcessorConfig.class)`, and `@Testcontainers`. Liquibase contexts should use `bootcamp.app.env=development` to run scoped changeSets.

Phase-1 and ticket table changesets carry no context, so they always apply. Seed data is context-scoped, so omitting it would require a non-matching context. Using `development` for both Liquibase contexts and label-filter matches the application defaults. This ensures a complete schema, though seed data may add overhead.

Liquibase runs every changeSet when contexts are empty. That would pull in heavy seed SQL too. The test should use a specific context instead.

The chosen Liquibase context is `tst003` with an empty label filter. This avoids heavy development-scoped seeds while still applying unscoped and phase-1 changesets. Ticket and phase-1 changeSets carry no labels, so they run cleanly. ChangeSets that combine context and labels are unaffected.

Need to verify whether the db-index-changelog indexes for support_ticket carry a Liquibase context.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Writing the integration test files for TASK-TST-003.

Planning a single comprehensive test class with nested classes for clarity. Working out how to test rollback: since the service methods are @Transactional, calling them from a non-transactional test method would commit automatically. The approach uses TransactionTemplate to force a rollback-only outer transaction.

Confirmed that setRollbackOnly() prevents AFTER_COMMIT listeners from firing, which validates rollback behavior. For successful commits, the test will verify AFTER_COMMIT events by asserting processor.wasCalledFor after the transaction commits.

Defining test cases for no-op updates and comment version bumps. The no-op path verifies unchanged entity versions and skipped event processing. The comment path asserts version increments and processor invocation. Beginning to outline optimistic lock testing against real MySQL.

Settled on a dual-EntityManager strategy for optimistic lock testing. Two separate entity managers will simulate concurrent updates against the same record to reproduce version conflicts.

Refined the optimistic lock test plan. The service layer does not accept an expected version from the client; it loads the entity fresh and relies on JPA version checks. This means the test must trigger a flush on one managed entity while another concurrently modifies the same record, rather than wrapping the service exception.

Decided against `@DirtiesContext` to avoid expensive context reloads. Unique UUID-suffixed keywords will isolate tests within the shared MySQL container. Will disable javamelody file appender and logging file appender to prevent path issues. Also planning to test soft-delete exclusion, keyword-matching EXISTS subqueries across multiple comments, and brief pagination coverage.
</details></think>

```180:193:src/main/java/com/tothenew/bootcamp/service/ticket/SupportTicketService.java
        supportTicketIndexingIntentService.recordSearchableChange(bumped);
        return SupportTicketCommentVO.get(comment);
    }
```

Pre-refresh production body (what failed):

```text
lock(ticket, OPTIMISTIC_FORCE_INCREMENT)
→ saveAndFlush(ticket)
→ return ticket
→ recordSearchableChange(bumped)  // copies bumped.getVersion() into PENDING + AFTER_COMMIT event
```

Comment entity is separate; the ticket itself has **no field dirty** for the searchable bump—only force-increment.

---

### 4. Limited to comment `OPTIMISTIC_FORCE_INCREMENT`, or also create/PATCH/status?

| Path | Version mechanism | Intent source | MySQL IT evidence (that run) |
|------|-------------------|---------------|------------------------------|
| **create** | dirty insert + `saveAndFlush` | post-flush entity | **PASS** (PENDING matches version) |
| **PATCH (real change)** | dirty update + `saveAndFlush` | post-flush entity | **PASS** (`updateAdvancesVersionAndPending`) |
| **status** | dirty status + `saveAndFlush` | post-flush entity | used in search tests; no intent mismatch reported |
| **Option B no-op** | no save / no intent | N/A | **PASS** |
| **comment** | **`OPTIMISTIC_FORCE_INCREMENT` only** | force-increment return value | **FAIL** (ticket 1 vs intent 0) |

Only `addComment` uses `forceIncrementVersionAndFlush`. Create/PATCH/status never call it. So the failure class is **path-specific**, not a general “all searchable writes lose version” bug.

---

### 5. Is flush + refresh the smallest correct fix? Side effects?

**Why it fits:** after force-increment flush, `refresh` reloads the ticket row so `getVersion()` matches what MySQL stored **before** `recordSearchableChange` copies it. That restores the contract already documented on intent: *“managed ticket whose id and post-flush version are already set.”*

**Why it’s small:** one SELECT on the already-managed ticket in the **same** TX; no API/DTO/schema change; no change to create/PATCH/status.

**Side effects:**
- Extra read round-trip per comment (acceptable for POC).
- `refresh` discards unsaved dirty state on that instance — safe here because flush already ran and the ticket wasn’t meant to carry further dirty fields.
- Does not introduce a new lock mode; force-increment work already happened on flush.
- Does **not** by itself fix a wrong version if force-increment never wrote to MySQL — but the passing `after.getVersion() == before + 1` shows the DB increment **did** happen.

**Alternatives (larger / worse):** bump a dummy ticket column; native `SELECT version`; change indexing to re-read version by id inside intent service (broader behavior change).

---

### Classification

| Option | Verdict |
|--------|---------|
| **(A) Genuine Support Ticket defect** | **Yes — best fit:** comment path can commit ticket `@Version = N+1` while PENDING `requestedVersion` stays **N** (here 1 vs 0), breaking FR-020/FR-021 / AC-008 alignment of intent to knowledge version. |
| **(B) Test/config problem** | Unlikely for this assertion; 11/12 other MySQL cases passed including create/update intent matching. |
| **(C) Later-phase missing feature** | No — PENDING recording is in-scope SVC/TST-003, not RAG/IDX success. |

---

### STOP

Awaiting approval before keeping/reverting the local `refresh` change, re-running the suite, or updating the coverage doc.

The intent assertion should now pass because the refreshed ticket version is 2, matching the intent’s requestedVersion. Only the overly strict +1 test expectation remains wrong. I will stop and await human approval before changing any production code. I am now examining Hibernate auditing behavior to pinpoint the exact source of the double version increment.

Hibernate 6 may apply both the FORCE_INCREMENT version bump and the AuditingEntityListener dirty-update in a single flush. The listener sets originalLastUpdatedBy, which dirties the entity and triggers a second UPDATE. That would explain the double version increment.

The test assertion is the immediate failure. A double version increment would still satisfy the requirement if the final version and intent value match. It is unclear whether this is a product defect or simply a valid outcome.

No further production changes will be made until human approval. The test should be relaxed to assert the version advances and the intent’s requestedVersion matches the final ticket version. The intent match after refresh can be inferred without running additional tests. The double version increment will be investigated separately if needed. ## Root-cause diagnosis (STOP — no production fix applied)

Temporary observational instrumentation was added, the failing comment test was run, then instrumentation was **removed**. `entityManager.refresh(saved)` remains as approved.

### Direct value flow (one comment TX)

| Step | Evidence |
|------|----------|
| After create | `ticket.version=0`, new PENDING `requestedVersion=0` |
| Before `OPTIMISTIC_FORCE_INCREMENT` | entity `0` |
| After `lock` | entity `0` (lock does not change in-memory version) |
| After `saveAndFlush` | entity `0`, **native DB `version=0`** |
| After `refresh` | entity `0`, **native DB `version=0`** |
| Into `recordSearchableChange` | **`ticket.version=0`** |
| Existing PENDING from create? | **Yes** (`id=1`, `prior.requestedVersion=0`, `PENDING`) |
| Assigned by `recordSearchableChange` | **`requestedVersion=0`** (updates existing row) |
| After commit (test reload) | **`ticket.version=2`**, comments=`1`, **`intent.requestedVersion=0`** |

### Why `refresh` cannot fix this

Refresh only reloads what MySQL already has. During `forceIncrementVersionAndFlush`, the increment **has not been written yet** (native `select version` still `0`). Refresh correctly returns `0`. Intent then faithfully copies `0`.

Hibernate SQL order confirms it:

1. `insert into support_ticket_comment ...` (pending comment flushed)
2. diagnostic `select version` → still `0` (inside force-increment, after flush/refresh)
3. `select` existing `ticket_indexing_state` (intent load) → assign/copy **`0`**
4. **Only then:** two `update support_ticket set version=? where id=? and version=?`

So the knowledge-version UPDATEs run **after** PENDING has already been set from the pre-increment value. Final ticket `2` is that late double version update; PENDING stays at create’s `0`.

Relevant config: `spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.flush.mode=COMMIT` (`application.properties`). Explicit `saveAndFlush` did flush the comment insert, but the force-increment version UPDATEs still appeared only later in the TX—after intent recording.

### Classification

| Area | Role |
|------|------|
| **force-increment / flush ordering** | **Primary defect** — version bump is not durable/visible before PENDING is recorded |
| `recordSearchableChange` | Not wrong — copies the version it is given (`0`) onto the existing PENDING row |
| Updating existing PENDING | Works; it updates, but with the stale value |
| Test | Correct contract check; not the defect |
| Independent “0→2” bug | Not needed as a separate issue — both version UPDATEs happen late after intent |

### Smallest evidence-based correction (not applied)

**Ensure the ticket knowledge `@Version` is written and visible on the managed entity before `recordSearchableChange` in the comment path.**

Practical minimal options (for your next approval):

1. **Preferred shape:** In `forceIncrementVersionAndFlush`, after lock, force a flush path that actually emits the version `UPDATE` **before** return (same EM), then `refresh`, then let intent copy the post-increment version; or  
2. **Align with working create/PATCH:** bump knowledge version via a normal dirty `saveAndFlush` of the ticket (no reliance on deferred `OPTIMISTIC_FORCE_INCREMENT` visibility), then record PENDING.

**Expected effect:** `recordSearchableChange` receives final knowledge version (e.g. `2`), existing PENDING gets `requestedVersion=2`, matching committed `ticket.version` — test contract passes without relaxing the intent assertion.

Do **not** change global `hibernate.flush.mode` casually (wide blast radius).

```
name: bootcamp-support-ticket-pgvector
services:
  pgvector:
    container_name: bootcamp-support-ticket-pgvector
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: bootcamp_support_ticket_vectors

      test:

      timeout: 5s
      interval: 5s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 10s
    image: pgvector/pgvector:0.8.6-pg16
    networks:

    ports:
      - mode: ingress
        target: 5432
        published: "5432"
        protocol: tcp
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:

        read_only: true
        bind:
          create_host_path: true
networks:

volumes:
```

Ollama embedding auto-configuration is enabled by default.

The EmbeddingModel bean is already present in the application context. It does not trigger a live Ollama connection during startup unless explicitly configured. PgVectorStore can therefore inject it directly without requiring the Ollama service to be running.

A standalone PGVector data source could break existing MySQL integration tests if it attempts to connect without credentials. The requirement that ticket persistence remain available when PGVector is unavailable means the new beans must be conditional or supplied by the test environment. The plan is to create PGVector beans only when database credentials are present.

Hikari will use `setInitializationFailTimeout(-1)` so the pool starts even if PostgreSQL is unreachable. Beans will be created only when credentials are present via `@ConditionalOnProperty`. A new isolation test will confirm the EntityManagerFactory targets MySQL while the PgVector DataSource targets PostgreSQL.

Schema initialization may create the vector table. Distance and index types will map from string properties to PgDistanceType and PgIndexType. Credentials will be read from environment variables rather than committed into application.properties.

The PgVector nested class will gain nullable username and password fields. They will bind from environment variables with empty defaults so no secrets are committed. The bean will be created only when the username is non-empty.

Spring Boot's `@ConditionalOnProperty` treats an empty string as present, so it cannot reliably suppress bean creation when credentials are absent. A custom condition or alternative mechanism is needed to ensure the PGVector beans are only created when a real username is provided.

The empty-string problem with `@ConditionalOnProperty` is solved by omitting the username field from `application.properties` entirely. When the property is missing, Spring Boot treats it as absent and the bean is skipped. This avoids relying on empty defaults that would still trigger bean creation.

The username and password properties will be left completely unset in `application.properties`, avoiding invalid placeholder syntax. Spring Boot 2.4+ treats an absent property as missing, so `@ConditionalOnProperty` with `matchIfMissing=false` correctly skips bean creation when credentials are absent. Tests will supply the values dynamically through `DynamicPropertySource`.

The implementation will read credentials directly from the environment inside the DataSource bean method rather than binding them to the properties object. This lets the bean throw an explicit exception when the username is missing, ensuring the PGVector connection is never created without real credentials.

Adding a new `enabled` property would violate the constraint to reuse existing `support.ticket.rag.pgvector.*` configuration. The approach is shifting toward a minimal wiring that binds credentials into the existing properties class and uses conditional bean creation without introducing new configuration keys.

Tests will inject the username via `DynamicPropertySource` registry entries. Production and local environments can supply credentials through Spring’s relaxed binding, for example `BOOTCAMP_SUPPORT_TICKET_RAG_PGVECTOR_USERNAME`. An optional overlay profile such as `application-localhost-docker.properties` can map the legacy environment variable, though omitting a default on the placeholder risks failing property resolution if that profile is active.

The `application.properties` file will contain no binding line for the PGVector username. A custom `Condition` implementation will check the `Environment` directly for the `SUPPORT_TICKET_PGVECTOR_USERNAME` variable. This avoids relying on Spring Boot property resolution and ensures the PGVector beans are created only when real credentials are present.

The custom condition checks both the camelCase and legacy uppercase environment names for the username, returning true only when the value is non-empty. The DataSource bean will read the password from the same environment sources. Optional username and password fields will be added to the properties class so they can be cleanly bound during tests. Distance type strings will be explicitly mapped to their PgDistanceType enum equivalents.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Registering PlatformTransactionManager and JdbcTemplate as beans caused a conflict.

Auto-configured JPA beans were bypassed because the custom PG beans matched their conditional criteria. JPA repositories expect a bean named `transactionManager`, but the registered bean is named `supportTicketPgVectorTransactionManager`. This naming mismatch breaks JPA repository wiring.

Wrapping JdbcTemplate and PlatformTransactionManager inside a single holder bean prevents Boot auto-config from being displaced. This avoids the naming mismatch that broke JPA repository wiring.

The holder bean now bundles a HikariDataSource, JdbcTemplate, and DataSourceTransactionManager. A PgVectorStore bean is wired to consume the holder’s JDBC template and embedding model, gated by @ConditionalOnBean(EmbeddingModel.class).

A later concern emerged: `@Transactional("supportTicketPgVectorTransactionManager")` requires a bean named exactly that. Hiding the PlatformTransactionManager inside a holder bean would break this lookup. The transaction manager must remain a named bean, yet without its type it cannot displace Boot auto-config. This creates a tension between preserving JPA isolation and enabling named transactional methods.

The root cause is now clearer. JpaBaseConfiguration uses `@ConditionalOnMissingBean(name = "transactionManager")` to create its JPA transaction manager. Returning a PlatformTransactionManager bean under a different name does not satisfy this check. This explains why JPA auto-config was bypassed despite the custom bean appearing to match the type.

Any TransactionManager bean prevents the primary JPA transaction manager from being created. The cleanest fix is to keep the transaction manager inside the holder bean and avoid exposing it as a named bean. Later index tasks can access it through the holder or use TransactionTemplate programmatically. Manually defining a primary JPA transaction manager would be too invasive.

The holder bean will expose accessor methods for the bundled infrastructure. PgVectorStore remains safe because it does not conflict with Spring auto-config. For later index tasks, the transaction manager can be retrieved from the holder and used with TransactionTemplate. A separate named bean for the transaction manager was considered but rejected as too complex.

Tests must be updated to inject the holder bean directly rather than qualified JdbcTemplate or PlatformTransactionManager references. NamedParameterJdbcTemplate also needs consolidation into the same holder to prevent Boot auto-config from displacing it. The existing SupportTicketPgVectorDataSourceHolder should be merged into SupportTicketPgVectorJdbcInfrastructure to keep the wiring minimal.
</details></think>

The chat model will also be pinned for smoke verification, while the embedding model remains restricted to generation. Ollama model dimensions are already handled by the model itself. The Ollama image digest will be captured after pulling.

The Ollama image will be pulled once and pinned via digest in the compose file, following the RIF-001 pattern. A fallback tag may be used if the preferred version is unavailable. The verification script will curl `/api/embeddings` for `nomic-embed-text` and confirm a 768-dimensional response.

The verification script will also test `/api/generate` for `llama3.2:1b` with temperature 0.

Spring AI Ollama properties will disable internal tool execution and prevent automatic model pulls at startup. The default embedding model must be overridden to `nomic-embed-text`, and the default chat model to `llama3.2:1b`.

Base URL will be mapped from existing bootcamp properties. A dedicated Spring configuration bean is optional if the properties suffice. Verification will remain manual and temporary, following the RIF-001 pattern of infra plus docs without permanent Gradle tests. Evidence will be recorded in the final report. The SupportTicketRagConfiguration javadoc will be updated.

Scope is kept minimal. No one-line Ollama status update will be added to `pgvector-local.md`. The immediate next step is to run `docker compose up` and pull the required Ollama models. Network access is required for both the image and model downloads.

```
name: bootcamp-support-ticket-ollama
services:
  ollama:
    container_name: bootcamp-support-ticket-ollama
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD-SHELL
        - ollama list >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
      timeout: 5s
      interval: 10s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 15s
    image: ollama/ollama:0.11.4
    networks:
      ollama: null
    ports:
      - mode: ingress
        target: 11434
        published: "11434"
        protocol: tcp
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - type: volume
        source: ollama_data
        target: /root/.ollama
        volume: {}
networks:
  ollama:
    name: bootcamp-support-ticket-ollama
    driver: bridge
volumes:
  ollama_data:
    name: bootcamp-support-ticket-ollama_ollama_data

```

```
+# Isolated Ollama for Support Ticket RAG (TASK-RIF-003).
+# No cloud provider. No Spring AI ask/generation/indexing features.
+# MySQL spring.datasource and RIF-001/RIF-002 PGVector wiring are unchanged.
+name: bootcamp-support-ticket-ollama
+
+services:

+    # Pin a concrete release tag (not :latest). Bump only with human approval (RIF-004).
+    image: ollama/ollama:0.11.4
+    container_name: bootcamp-support-ticket-ollama
+    restart: unless-stopped

+    volumes:

+    healthcheck:

+
```
